Solve an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the 74-bus distribution system model `case74ds`. Before running the OPF, modify the network data as follows:

1) At bus 5, tighten the lower bound on the voltage magnitude by setting the minimum allowable voltage magnitude VMIN to 0.99 per unit, so the bus voltage cannot drop below 0.99 p.u. in the optimization.

2) For all generators connected at bus 10, modify their quadratic generation cost characteristics by scaling the cubic (third-order) active power cost coefficient (the C3 term in the polynomial cost function) by a factor of 0, effectively setting that highest-order cost coefficient to zero. This removes the cubic dependence of operating cost on active power for generators at bus 10, leaving only lower-order terms (if present) in their cost functions.

3) For the transmission line (or distribution feeder) that directly connects bus 14 and bus 70, adjust the total line charging susceptance by scaling the branch shunt susceptance parameter BR_B by a factor of 1.2 in both directions. This increases the line charging susceptance between bus 14 and bus 70 by 20% relative to its original value.

After applying these modifications, run an ACOPF using MATPOWER with the OPF violation tolerance parameter `opf.violation` set to 1e-6, and print the resulting power flow and optimization summary.

Perform an AC optimal power flow on the IEEE 9-bus test system (case9). Before solving, modify the quadratic active power cost coefficient of the generator connected at bus 3 by scaling it to 80% of its original value. Concretely, multiply the third-order cost coefficient (the quadratic term in the generator cost function) for all generators located at bus 3 by a factor of 0.8, leaving all other cost parameters and network data unchanged. Use an OPF violation tolerance of 1e-6 when running the ACOPF.

Formulate and solve an AC optimal power flow problem for the MATPOWER microgrid test system case33mg. First, reduce the active power demand at bus 18 by scaling its original active load by a factor of 0.9, thereby decreasing the real power consumption at that bus by 10%. Next, modify the reactive power capability of the generator connected to bus 1 by setting its minimum reactive power output limit to -50 MVAr, allowing it to absorb up to 50 MVAr of reactive power. Then, adjust the resistance of the transmission branch that electrically connects bus 14 and bus 22 by multiplying its original series resistance value by 1.1, increasing the branch resistance by 10% in both directions of power flow (14–22 and 22–14). After these network parameter changes, solve the AC optimal power flow on the modified case33mg system using an OPF violation tolerance of 1e-7, and print the resulting power flow and optimal dispatch report.

Run an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the modified case9Q system. First, adjust the reactive power demand at bus 2 by increasing it by 10%, i.e., scale the reactive power demand at bus 2 by a factor of 1.1. Then tighten the upper voltage magnitude limit at bus 1 by scaling its maximum allowable voltage magnitude by a factor of 1.02 relative to its original value. For the transmission element connecting bus 6 and bus 4, enforce the in-service status by setting its branch status flag to 1, treating this line as fully in service in both directions (6–4 and 4–6 if present). Finally, solve the ACOPF with an OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) set to 1e-7.

Run an AC optimal power flow on the IEEE 118-bus test system (case118). Before solving, modify the network data as follows. At bus 59, scale the maximum allowable bus voltage magnitude (VMAX) by a factor of 1.05, thereby increasing the upper voltage limit at that specific bus by 5% relative to its original value. For the generator located at bus 12, increase the generator’s maximum reactive power output limit (QMAX) by multiplying its original value by 1.2, effectively raising its reactive power capability at that bus by 20%. Use an OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) of 1e-6 in the MATPOWER options, then execute the ACOPF and print the resulting power flow and OPF solution report.

Run an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the 30-bus reactive power test system case30Q. First, modify the shunt susceptance at bus 15 by setting its shunt susceptance (BS) to 0.2 per unit. Then adjust two transmission elements: for the branch connecting bus 9 and bus 30, double its series resistance by multiplying the existing branch resistance by a factor of 2.0; and for the branch between bus 23 and bus 18, increase its total line charging susceptance by 20% by multiplying the existing susceptance value (BR_B) by 1.2. After applying these changes, solve the ACOPF using an OPF constraint violation tolerance (opf.violation) of 1e-6 and report the resulting power flow and optimal dispatch.

Using the IEEE 85-bus network defined in MATPOWER as case85, set up and solve an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF). Before running the OPF, increase the reactive power demand at bus 35 by 10% by scaling its original reactive demand value by a factor of 1.1. Additionally, reduce the maximum active power output capability of the generator connected at bus 7 by 10% by multiplying its original maximum active power limit by 0.9. Solve the ACOPF with an OPF constraint violation tolerance of 1e-6, and then print the resulting power flow and optimization summary.

Perform an AC optimal power flow on the IEEE 145-bus test system defined in MATPOWER as 'case145'. Before running the OPF, modify the network as follows. At bus 57, tighten the minimum allowable voltage magnitude by setting the lower voltage bound to 0.98 pu. For the generator connected at bus 8, reduce its reactive power capability on the upper side by scaling its maximum reactive power output limit to 80% of its original value. For the generator located at bus 17, decrease its linear active power generation cost coefficient (the C1 term in the cost function) to 80% of its initial value, thus making its marginal cost 20% lower. For the transmission element that connects bus 110 and bus 103, ensure that this branch is in service by explicitly setting its status to 1. Finally, solve the ACOPF with an OPF constraint violation tolerance of 1e-6 and print the resulting power flow and optimal dispatch.

Solve an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the IEEE 51-bus system modeled by the MATPOWER case file 'case51he'. Before running the OPF, enforce a minimum voltage magnitude of 1.0 p.u. at bus 2 by setting the lower voltage limit at that bus to 1.0 p.u. Modify the generator cost at all generators connected to bus 3 by scaling the quadratic active power cost coefficient (the C2 term in the quadratic cost curve) by a factor of 0.9, thereby reducing the curvature of their cost function while leaving the linear and constant terms unchanged. For the transmission element that electrically connects bus 39 and bus 21, scale its series reactance by a factor of 0, effectively setting the branch reactance to zero while keeping all other branch parameters as originally specified. Finally, perform the ACOPF with the OPF constraint violation tolerance set to 1e-8 via the 'opf.violation' option in MATPOWER, and print the resulting power flow and OPF solution report.

Run an AC optimal power flow on the MATPOWER 300‑bus test system (case300). Before solving, modify the network data as follows. First, at bus 41, increase the reactive power demand by scaling its original value by a factor of 1.2, i.e., the reactive load at bus 41 is increased by 20%. Second, for the transmission element that directly connects bus 249 and bus 36, set its total line charging susceptance to zero by multiplying the existing susceptance value by a factor of 0, effectively removing the shunt charging on that branch. Use an OPF constraint violation tolerance (opf.violation) of 1e-7 when running the AC optimal power flow.

Solve an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the IEEE 39-bus test system (case39). Before running the OPF, modify the network data as follows. At bus 38, set the shunt susceptance (the BS term representing shunt reactive admittance to ground) to 0.2 per unit. For the transmission line connecting bus 2 and bus 38, scale the branch total line charging susceptance (BR_B) by a factor of 1.1, applying this scaling to that specific branch regardless of its recorded direction (2-to-38 or 38-to-2). Use an OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) of 1e-6 in the MATPOWER options, then run the ACOPF and print the resulting power flow and OPF solution.

Solve an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the IEEE 5-bus system (case5). Before running the OPF, modify the shunt susceptance of the transmission line that directly connects bus 1 and bus 3. Specifically, identify the branch whose from-bus is 1 and to-bus is 3 (or equivalently from-bus 3 to-bus 1, since the line is bidirectional), and scale its total line charging susceptance (the BR_B parameter in MATPOWER, representing the line’s shunt susceptance) by a factor of 0, effectively setting the line charging susceptance on that corridor to zero. Use an OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) of 1e-8, then execute the ACOPF and print the resulting power flow and OPF summary.

Solve an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the IEEE 22-bus system represented by case22. Before running the OPF, modify the network data as follows.

First, at bus 8, set the minimum allowable voltage magnitude to 1.0 per unit. This tightens the lower bound on the bus voltage so that during the OPF solution the voltage magnitude at bus 8 cannot drop below 1.0 p.u.

Second, for all generators connected to bus 4, set the minimum reactive power output to -50 MVAr. This change constrains each generator at bus 4 so that its reactive power injection cannot be less than -50 MVAr (i.e., it cannot absorb more than 50 MVAr).

Third, for all generators connected to bus 1, scale the cubic coefficient (the coefficient of the P^3 term) of their active power generation cost function by a factor of 1.1. This operation increases the third-order cost coefficient by 10% for every generator at bus 1, making high active power outputs from these units slightly more expensive in the OPF objective.

Fourth, for the transmission line(s) connecting bus 2 and bus 21, identified in the branch data regardless of direction (either from bus 2 to bus 21 or from bus 21 to bus 2), scale the branch series resistance by a factor of 0. This effectively sets the series resistance of each such branch to zero, removing active power losses associated with the ohmic resistance on that connection.

Finally, set the OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) to 1e-6 to enforce a relatively tight tolerance on constraint violations, and then run the ACOPF on this modified case22 system, printing the full power flow and OPF results.

Run an AC optimal power flow on the IEEE 30-bus test system (case30) with specific network and voltage limit adjustments. First, at bus 19, set the minimum allowable voltage magnitude to 0.85 per unit, tightening the lower voltage bound at that bus. Next, at bus 17, scale the maximum allowable voltage magnitude by a factor of 1.08, increasing its upper voltage limit to 1.08 times its original value. For the transmission element connecting buses 24 and 11, scale the branch series reactance by a factor of 0, effectively setting its reactance to zero while maintaining its resistance and other parameters unchanged. For the branch between buses 2 and 19, set the transformer off-nominal tap ratio to 0, directly assigning the tap ratio to zero for that specific branch. After applying all these modifications, solve the AC optimal power flow using an OPF violation tolerance of 1e-8.

Solve an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the IEEE 14-bus test system (case14). Before running the OPF, modify the series resistance of the transmission line connecting bus 10 and bus 2. Specifically, scale the branch resistance (BR_R), which represents the series active power loss component of the line impedance, for the line between bus 10 and bus 2 (treating it as an undirected connection between buses 10 and 2) by a factor of 0, effectively setting its series resistance to zero. Use an OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) of 1e-08 in the MATPOWER options when running the ACOPF.

Solve an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) problem on the distribution test system defined in MATPOWER as case33bw. First, modify the reactive power demand at bus 21 by increasing it by 10%, i.e., scale the existing reactive power demand at bus 21 by a factor of 1.1. Next, modify the shunt susceptance at bus 14 by directly setting its value to -0.1 per unit, representing a shunt element with negative susceptance connected at that bus. After applying these two changes to the network data, run the AC optimal power flow with the OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) set to 1e-8.

Run an AC optimal power flow on the 70-bus system specified in case70da. Before solving, modify the network data as follows. For bus 14, increase the maximum allowable voltage magnitude by scaling its VMAX value by a factor of 1.02, effectively relaxing the upper voltage limit at that bus by 2%. At bus 35, fix the minimum allowable voltage magnitude by setting VMIN to exactly 0.95 per unit, tightening the lower voltage bound at that location. For the transmission line connecting bus 27 and bus 44, reduce its continuous thermal rating by scaling the RATE_A value to 75% of its original value, thereby lowering the maximum permissible active power flow on that branch. Use an OPF constraint violation tolerance (opf.violation) of 1e-8 when running the ACOPF, and print the resulting power flow and OPF solution.

Run an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the IEEE 57-bus test system (case57). Before solving, modify the network data by scaling the maximum allowable voltage magnitude at bus 57 by a factor of 1.02, thereby increasing its original upper voltage limit by 2%. Use an OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) of 1e-08 in the solver settings, then execute the ACOPF and print the resulting power flow and optimization report.

Run an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the IEEE RTS 24-bus test system using the MATPOWER case file case24_ieee_rts. Before solving the OPF, modify the reactive power capability of the generator(s) connected at bus 4 by scaling their maximum reactive power output QMAX to 80% of their original values, i.e., multiply each QMAX at bus 4 by a factor of 0.8. Use an OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) of 1e-8 in the solver options, then execute the OPF and print the resulting power flow and dispatch report.

Run an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the IEEE 18-bus test system (case18). Before solving, modify the network data as follows:

1) At bus 9, scale the active power demand to zero by multiplying its original active power demand by a factor of 0, effectively removing the active load at this bus.

2) For all generators connected to bus 2, reduce the cubic coefficient of their active power generation cost function to 90% of its original value. Concretely, multiply the third-order (cubic) cost coefficient (C3 term in the polynomial cost curve) for every generator at bus 2 by 0.9, while keeping all other cost coefficients unchanged.

3) For the transmission line(s) connecting bus 7 and bus 13, increase the total line charging susceptance by 20%. Specifically, identify every branch whose endpoints are buses 7 and 13 (in either direction) and multiply its line charging susceptance parameter by 1.2.

Finally, solve the ACOPF with the OPF violation tolerance set to 1e-7, and print the resulting power flow and OPF solution report.

Solve an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the modified case118zh system. In the generation cost model for all generators located at bus 20, scale the linear cost coefficient (the C1 term of the polynomial active power cost function) by a factor of 1.2, thereby increasing their marginal cost of active power output by 20%. For every generator connected to bus 3, keep the reactive power capability unchanged by multiplying the maximum reactive power output limit Qmax by a factor of 1.0. In the transmission network, open the line between bus 85 and bus 11 by setting its branch status to 0, effectively removing this branch from service in both directions. For the transmission line connecting bus 66 and bus 85, increase the series reactance by 10% by multiplying its branch reactance by a factor of 1.1; this is applied regardless of the direction (66–85 or 85–66). Use an OPF violation tolerance of 1e-7 in the MATPOWER options, run the ACOPF with these modifications, and print the resulting power flow and OPF solution.

Using the MATPOWER case30pwl test system, set up and solve an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF). Before running the OPF, modify the transmission element that connects bus 13 and bus 29: increase its series reactance by 20% by multiplying the original branch reactance value by a factor of 1.2, applied symmetrically for the line between bus 13 and bus 29 regardless of direction. Configure the OPF solver with an inequality violation tolerance of 1×10⁻⁷, then execute the ACOPF and print the resulting power flow and optimal dispatch report.

Run an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the PEGASE 89-bus test system (case89pegase) with targeted modifications to specific buses and generators before solving. First, increase the active power demand at bus 69 by 10% by scaling its active load value by a factor of 1.1. Next, adjust the voltage magnitude lower limit at bus 29 so that its minimum allowable voltage magnitude is set to 1.0 per unit. For the generators, modify the linear term of the active power generation cost at all generators connected to bus 13 by multiplying their linear cost coefficient (the C1 term in the polynomial cost function) by 1.5, effectively increasing their marginal cost. Additionally, set the minimum active power output of all generators located at bus 8 to 20 MW. After applying these modifications, solve the ACOPF with an OPF violation tolerance set to 1e-8 and print the resulting power flow and optimization results.

For the modified IEEE 9-bus target system (case9target), perform an AC optimal power flow analysis. Before running the OPF, adjust the thermal rating of the transmission element that connects bus 6 and bus 4. Specifically, scale the continuous MVA rating (RATE_A) of this branch by a factor of 0.9, thereby reducing its allowable continuous apparent power flow to 90% of its original limit. Use an OPF constraint violation tolerance of 1e-6 in the solver settings, then solve the ACOPF and print the resulting power flow and optimal dispatch.

Formulate and solve an AC optimal power flow problem for the IEEE 69-bus test system defined in MATPOWER as case69. Before running the OPF, modify the network data as follows:

1. At bus 49, increase the upper limit on the bus voltage magnitude by scaling its existing maximum voltage magnitude by a factor of 1.1. This raises the allowable maximum per-unit voltage at bus 49 by 10% relative to its original value.
2. For the generator connected at bus 5, set its minimum active power output to 0 MW, effectively allowing this generator to operate down to zero active power injection if economically optimal.
3. For the transmission element connecting bus 4 and bus 40, scale its series resistance by a factor of 0, thereby setting the branch series resistance between buses 4 and 40 to zero while leaving all other branch parameters unchanged.

After applying these three specific modifications, solve the AC OPF with an OPF constraint violation tolerance set to 1e-7, and print the resulting power flow and OPF solution.

Perform an AC optimal power flow on the MATPOWER case `case94pi`. Before running the OPF, modify the network as follows.

First, at bus 28, scale the maximum allowable voltage magnitude limit by a factor of 1.04, thereby increasing the upper bound on the bus voltage magnitude to 1.04 times its original value.

Second, for the generator connected at bus 6, increase the cubic cost coefficient in its active power generation cost function by a factor of 1.5. This scales the third-order term of the generator’s polynomial cost curve, making high active power outputs more expensive.

Third, for the transmission element between bus 93 and bus 25, reduce its continuous MVA rating (RATE_A) to zero by multiplying the original thermal rating by a factor of 0. This effectively prohibits active and reactive power flow on that branch in the OPF solution.

Fourth, for the branch connecting bus 16 to bus 69, set the off-nominal tap ratio of the transformer to a fixed value of 0.975 per unit, thereby adjusting the voltage magnitude and power flow distribution through this transformer.

Finally, solve the AC optimal power flow with an OPF constraint violation tolerance set to 1e-7, and print the resulting power flow and OPF solution report.

Solve an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the MATPOWER case file 'case51ga'. Before running the OPF, modify the system as follows. For the generator located at bus 4, scale the quadratic coefficient (the coefficient on the squared active power output term) in its active power generation cost function by a factor of 1.2, thereby increasing the curvature of its cost curve by 20%. For the transformer or tap-changing branch that electrically connects bus 30 and bus 5, set its off-nominal turns ratio (tap ratio) to 1.05, fixing the magnitude of the tap at this value for all branches between these two buses regardless of direction. Then, run the ACOPF with the OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) set to 1e-06, and print the resulting power flow and OPF solution report.

Run an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the MATPOWER 6-bus Wood–Wollenberg test system (case6ww). First, modify the generator connected to bus 3 by setting its minimum reactive power output limit Qmin to -10 MVAr, so that this generator is allowed to absorb up to 10 MVAr of reactive power. Then, for the generator located at bus 1, reduce its maximum active power output limit Pmax by scaling the original value by a factor of 0.9, i.e., set the new maximum active power capability to 90% of its initial value. Next, adjust the thermal rating of the transmission line between bus 1 and bus 4: scale the continuous MVA rating (RATE_A) of this branch by a factor of 0.9, thereby reducing its allowable continuous apparent power flow to 90% of the original rating. Additionally, modify the series resistance of the branch connecting bus 4 and bus 3 by multiplying its resistance by 1.5, increasing the line resistance to 150% of its initial value. After applying these modifications, solve the ACOPF using an OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) of 1e-7, and print the resulting power flow and OPF solution report.

Solve an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the IEEE 141-bus system represented by the MATPOWER case file 'case141'. First, modify the generator located at bus 4 by setting its minimum active power output (Pmin) to 0 MW, effectively allowing this unit to reduce its active power generation down to zero if economically optimal. Next, adjust the quadratic cost coefficient of the generator at bus 26 by scaling its second-order active power cost term (the C2 coefficient in its polynomial generation cost function) by a factor of 0.8, thereby reducing the curvature of its cost curve and making higher outputs relatively less expensive. Use an OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) of 1e-8 when running the ACOPF, and print the resulting power flow and OPF solution.

For the MATPOWER case 'case136ma', perform an AC optimal power flow study with specific network adjustments. First, at bus 73, reduce the reactive power demand to 90% of its original value by multiplying the existing reactive load at this bus by a factor of 0.9. Next, modify the tap setting of the transformer or phase-shifting branch that connects bus 77 and bus 28: set its tap ratio parameter to 0, applying this change regardless of whether the branch is modeled from bus 77 to bus 28 or from bus 28 to bus 77 in the case file. After these modifications, solve the ACOPF using an OPF constraint violation tolerance of 1e-7 and print the resulting power flow and optimal dispatch.

Formulate and solve an AC optimal power flow problem for the case74ds power system. Modify the network data before running the OPF as follows. First, at bus 34, reduce the active power demand by scaling its original value by a factor of 0.8, so the real power load at this bus is decreased by 20% relative to the base case. Second, at bus 14, slightly relax the upper voltage magnitude limit by multiplying its original maximum allowable voltage magnitude by 1.01, increasing the permissible bus voltage ceiling by 1%. Third, for the transmission element connecting bus 45 and bus 41, reduce its continuous MVA rating (the RATE_A thermal limit) by scaling the existing rating by 0.9, thereby lowering its allowable continuous apparent power flow by 10%. After these modifications, solve an AC optimal power flow with an OPF constraint violation tolerance set to 1e-8, and print the resulting power flow and OPF solution summary.

Run an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the IEEE 9-bus test system (case9). Before solving the OPF, modify the generator and branch data as follows. For the generator located at bus 3, set its minimum reactive power output limit Qmin to -10 MVAr, thereby allowing it to absorb up to 10 MVAr of reactive power. For the transmission line connecting bus 7 and bus 8, scale its series resistance (branch active power resistance BR_R) by a factor of 0, effectively setting the resistance of that branch to zero while leaving all other branch parameters unchanged. Use an OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) of 1e-6 in the MATPOWER options, then solve the ACOPF and print the resulting power flow and dispatch.

Run an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the MATPOWER microgrid test case 'case33mg'. Before solving, modify the network data as follows. At bus 21, scale the maximum allowable voltage magnitude by a factor of 1.07, effectively increasing the upper voltage limit at that bus by 7%. For all generators connected at bus 3, scale their maximum active power output limits by a factor of 1.1, increasing each generator’s active power capability at that bus by 10%. For the branch that electrically connects bus 19 and bus 9, set the transformer tap ratio to 1.0 per unit (enforcing a nominal tap setting) for that line, regardless of its original value and considering the connection as bidirectional between bus 19 and bus 9. Use an OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) of 1e-8 when running the ACOPF, and then print the resulting power flow and optimal dispatch.

Run an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the case9Q test system. Modify the generator connected at bus 2 in two ways: first, increase the quadratic active power cost coefficient (the C2 term in the polynomial generation cost function) by scaling its original value by a factor of 1.5; second, tighten its reactive power capability on the under‑excited side by setting its minimum reactive power output Qmin to −30 MVAr. In the transmission network, adjust the thermal limit of the line between bus 4 and bus 8 by scaling its continuous MVA rating (RATE_A) to 90% of its original value, thereby reducing the allowable apparent power flow on that branch. Use an OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) of 1e-7 when solving the ACOPF, and print the resulting power flow and OPF solution report.

Run an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the IEEE 118-bus test system (case118) with specific adjustments to generator cost coefficients and branch parameters before solving. For the generator(s) connected at bus 20, multiply the quadratic active-power cost coefficient (the C3 term of the polynomial cost function) by 1.5, thereby increasing the sensitivity of operating cost to the square of active power output at that bus. For the generator(s) at bus 22, scale the constant term of the active-power cost function (the C1 coefficient) by 1.0, which leaves the constant component of the production cost unchanged. For the transmission line(s) between bus 28 and bus 70, scale the series resistance (BR_R) by a factor of 2.0, effectively doubling the line resistance and thus increasing resistive losses on that connection in both directions between these two buses. For the branch that connects bus 92 and bus 40, scale the continuous MVA rating (RATE_A) by 0.5, reducing its thermal capacity limit to half of its original value for power flow in either direction between these buses. After performing these modifications, solve the ACOPF with an OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) set to 1e-6, and print the resulting power flow and OPF solution report.

Run an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the MATPOWER test system case30Q. Before solving the OPF, modify the system data as follows. For the generator located at bus 2, reduce its maximum active power output limit by scaling it by a factor of 0.9, i.e., multiply the existing maximum active power capability at that generator by 0.9. For the generator connected at bus 5, set its minimum reactive power output limit to −10 MVAr, directly replacing the original lower reactive power bound. For the transmission element that connects bus 27 and bus 6, increase its series resistance by scaling the branch resistance by a factor of 1.5, considering the line regardless of direction (both 27–6 and 6–27). After applying these modifications, solve the AC optimal power flow with the OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) set to 1e-6, and print the resulting power flow and OPF solution report.

Run an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the IEEE 85-bus test system defined in case85. Before solving the OPF, modify the network data as follows. First, at bus 1, scale the maximum allowable voltage magnitude by a factor of 1.08, effectively increasing the upper voltage limit at that bus to 108% of its original value. Second, for the generator connected at bus 6, scale its maximum active power output limit (PMAX) by a factor of 1.0, which keeps the generator’s maximum active power capability numerically unchanged but explicitly applies the specified scaling operation. Third, for the branch that connects bus 34 and bus 65 (considering the line as bidirectional), set the transformer off-nominal tap ratio to 1.05, thereby adjusting the transformer tap to 1.05 per unit on that line. Configure the MATPOWER options so that the OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) is set to 1e-8, then run the ACOPF with these modified parameters and print the resulting power flow and OPF solution report.

Run an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the IEEE 145-bus test system defined in the MATPOWER case file 'case145'. Before solving the OPF, modify two elements of the network model. First, for bus 105, scale the maximum allowable voltage magnitude by a factor of 1.09, i.e., multiply the existing upper voltage limit at bus 105 by 1.09 so that the bus can operate at a higher maximum per-unit voltage than in the original case. Second, for the generator connected at bus 24, set its minimum active power output (Pmin) to 20 MW, replacing whatever minimum active power limit was originally specified for that unit. Use an OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) of 1e-6 in the MATPOWER options when solving the ACOPF, then execute the OPF and print the resulting power flow and dispatch summary.

Formulate and solve an AC optimal power flow for the 51-bus system defined in the MATPOWER case file `case51he`. Before running the OPF, impose the following parameter changes:

1. At bus 7, set the minimum allowable voltage magnitude to 0.9 per unit, tightening the lower voltage bound at that bus to 0.9 p.u.
2. At bus 28, scale the maximum allowable voltage magnitude by a factor of 1.06. This means the existing upper limit on the voltage magnitude at bus 28 is multiplied by 1.06, increasing its voltage upper bound accordingly.
3. For the generator connected at bus 7, scale the linear coefficient (the C1 term) of its active power generation cost function by a factor of 1.2. This multiplies the original linear cost coefficient by 1.2, effectively increasing the marginal cost slope associated with active power output at that generator.
4. For the transmission branch between bus 27 and bus 13, scale the series reactance by a factor of 1.2. The branch reactance on the line connecting buses 27 and 13 (considering it bidirectionally between these two buses) is multiplied by 1.2, increasing the line’s series reactance.

After these modifications, solve the AC optimal power flow using an OPF violation tolerance of 1e-7, and print the resulting power flow and OPF solution report.

Formulate and solve an AC optimal power flow on the IEEE 300‑bus system (MATPOWER case300). Modify the generation cost and reactive power limits, as well as one transmission element, before running the OPF:

1. For the generator connected at bus 58, scale the linear term of its active power cost function by a factor of 1.0. Since multiplying by 1.0 leaves the value unchanged, the linear cost coefficient for active power output at this unit remains exactly as originally specified in the case file.

2. For the generator at bus 11, scale the cubic term of its active power cost function by a factor of 0. This operation sets the cubic cost coefficient for active power generation at this unit to zero, effectively removing any third‑order dependence of the production cost on its active power output.

3. For the generator located at bus 60, set its minimum reactive power capability to −10 MVAr. This directly assigns the lower bound on the generator’s reactive power output to −10 MVAr, overriding whatever minimum reactive limit was originally defined.

4. For the transmission branch that electrically connects bus 2 and bus 200, scale its series reactance by a factor of 1.2. This increases the branch reactance by 20% relative to its original value, thereby altering the impedance of this specific line between buses 2 and 200.

After applying these modifications, run an AC optimal power flow on the modified case300 system using MATPOWER, with the OPF constraint violation tolerance set to 1e-6, and print the full power flow and OPF results.

Solve an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the IEEE 39-bus test system (case39). Before running the OPF, modify the reactive power demand at bus 22 by increasing it by 10%, i.e., scale the original reactive power demand at bus 22 by a factor of 1.1. Use an OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) of 1e-8 in the MATPOWER options, then run the ACOPF and print the resulting power flow and OPF solution.

Perform an AC optimal power flow on the IEEE 5-bus test system (MATPOWER case5). Before solving, modify the generator located at bus 3 in two ways. First, set its minimum reactive power output limit Qmin to -30 Mvar, tightening the lower bound on its reactive power capability. Second, scale the linear (first-order) active power cost coefficient of this same generator by a factor of 1.0, which leaves the original linear cost term unchanged. Use an OPF constraint violation tolerance of 1e-6 when configuring the MATPOWER solver, then run the ACOPF and print the power flow and OPF results.

Solve an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the IEEE 22-bus system represented by MATPOWER case file 'case22'. Before running the OPF, modify two specific transmission elements. First, for the branch that electrically connects bus 3 and bus 1, set the transformer off-nominal tap ratio to 0.975, affecting the voltage magnitude transformation between these two buses. Second, for the line between bus 20 and bus 19, set the branch status to 1 to ensure that this transmission line is energized and included in the network topology during the OPF calculation. Use an OPF violation tolerance of 1e-7 for the optimization constraints and then run the ACOPF and print the resulting power flow and dispatch summary.

Formulate and solve an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the IEEE 30-bus test system (case30). Before running the OPF, modify the series reactance of the transmission line that connects bus 9 and bus 22. Specifically, scale the branch reactance between bus 9 and bus 22 in both directions (i.e., treating the line as bidirectional) by a factor of 0.8, thereby reducing its reactance to 80% of its original value. Use an OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) of 1e-8 in the MATPOWER options, then execute the OPF and print the resulting power flow and optimization summary.

Solve an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the IEEE 14-bus test system (case14). Before running the OPF, modify the network data as follows: (1) At bus 10, scale the maximum allowable voltage magnitude by a factor of 1.02, so the voltage upper limit at this bus is increased by 2%. (2) At bus 3, set the shunt susceptance to exactly 0.1 per unit, thereby defining the reactive power shunt compensation at that bus. (3) For all generators connected at bus 3, scale their maximum reactive power output limits (QMAX) by a factor of 0.8, effectively reducing the reactive power capability at that location by 20%. (4) For the transmission branch that electrically connects bus 2 and bus 4 (in either direction), scale the total line charging susceptance (BR_B) by a factor of 1.1, increasing the shunt charging by 10% on that line. Use MATPOWER’s OPF solver with the OPF violation tolerance parameter (opf.violation) set to 1e-7, then run the ACOPF and print the resulting power flow and optimal dispatch report.

Using the MATPOWER distribution test case `case33bw`, set up and solve an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) problem. Before running the OPF, apply the following two modifications to the network model. First, at the generator located at bus 4, set its minimum active power output (PMIN) to 0 MW, effectively allowing the generator at bus 4 to reduce its active power injection down to zero if economically optimal. Second, disable the transmission line (branch) that connects bus 28 and bus 7 by setting its branch status to 0, which removes this line from service in the OPF formulation. Use an OPF violation tolerance of 1e-7 in the solver options, then run the ACOPF and print the resulting power flow and optimal dispatch summary.

Solve an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the MATPOWER case file case70da. Before running the OPF, modify the system data as follows:

1) At bus 26, increase the reactive power demand by 20% by scaling its original reactive power load (QD) value by a factor of 1.2.

2) For the transmission line connecting bus 1 and bus 67, reduce its continuous MVA rating (RATE_A) by 10% by multiplying the original RATE_A value by 0.9. The modification must apply regardless of whether the branch is stored with bus 1 as the from-bus and bus 67 as the to-bus, or vice versa.

After these modifications, run an ACOPF with the OPF constraint violation tolerance (opf.violation) set to 1e-7, and print the resulting power flow and OPF solution report.

Solve an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the IEEE 57-bus test system (case57). Before running the OPF, tighten the voltage magnitude lower bound at bus 51 by setting its minimum allowable voltage magnitude Vmin to 0.98 per unit. Also, modify the reactive power capability of the generator(s) connected at bus 5 by setting their minimum reactive power output Qmin to -50 MVAr. Use an OPF constraint violation tolerance (opf.violation) of 1e-7 when calling the MATPOWER solver.

Run an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the IEEE RTS 24-bus system (case24_ieee_rts). Before solving, modify two specific transmission elements. First, for the transformer or regulated branch connecting bus 6 and bus 10, set its off-nominal tap ratio to 0.975 per unit, adjusting the voltage transformation between these two buses. Second, for the branch connecting bus 23 and bus 18, scale its total line charging susceptance (the shunt susceptance associated with that branch) by a factor of 0, effectively setting its line charging susceptance to zero. Use an OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) of 1e-6 when running the ACOPF.

Run an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the 18-bus test system defined in case18. Before solving the OPF, increase the maximum active power output limit (PMAX) of all generators connected to bus 2 by 10%, i.e., multiply their existing maximum active power capability by a factor of 1.1. Also, adjust the cubic cost coefficient (the coefficient of the third-order active power term in the generator cost function) for all generators at bus 1 by scaling their existing third-order cost coefficient (C3) by a factor of 1.0, which effectively leaves this cost coefficient unchanged but is applied explicitly as specified. Set the OPF constraint violation tolerance (opf.violation) to 1e-8 when calling the solver, and then execute the ACOPF and print the full power flow and OPF results.
